# Phase 1 — Chesed Brainstorm: The Movie Studio Without Walls

> The Awtsmoos renews each frame from no prior frame;
> a timeline becomes a vessel, yet every app keeps its name.

## Mission
Reveal every 2D and 3D movie-making surface in `geelooy`, trace its actual runtime contracts, and converge duplicated capabilities onto one shared movie-creation grammar without flattening each app's distinct product identity.

## Required user outcomes
- AI can create a whole movie from structured intent rather than merely emit prose.
- 2D and 3D scenes share one scene/timeline contract where it is genuinely useful.
- Characters, shapes, text, infographic primitives, particles, cameras, transitions, audio hooks, and patches are composable.
- Movies can include many scenes, multiple camera angles, entrances/exits, animated typography, procedural motion, and deterministic timing.
- UI/UX is mobile-first while remaining productive on desktop.
- Existing apps remain recognizably different products even when they share the same engine.
- A real approximately three-minute showcase movie is authored and rendered/playback-tested.
- Verification includes syntax/static checks, runtime/browser checks, console inspection, and evidence that the full timeline reaches its end.

## Five architecture candidates
A. One giant universal editor: maximum reuse, unacceptable identity loss and coupling.
B. Shared schema only: safe but leaves rendering, AI, and timeline duplication.
C. Shared engine + app adapters: preferred if current app boundaries support it.
D. 2D and 3D completely separate engines: preserves specialization but prevents unified AI generation.
E. Plugin kernel with 2D/3D render backends: strongest long-term target if it can be introduced without breaking existing paths.

## Ideal capability universe
Scene graph; tracks; keyframes; easing; constraints; camera rigs; 2D canvas/SVG/DOM layers; 3D scene nodes; lights; materials; particle emitters; reusable characters; pose/motion clips; text; charts; infographic layouts; arrows; callouts; masks; transitions; audio cues; narration metadata; asset references; deterministic seeded procedural effects; AI-generated storyboards; AI-generated scene specs; validation; previews; timeline scrubbing; responsive stage; touch gestures; scene library; reusable templates; export/render hooks.

## Evidence required before code
- Exact app directories and entry points.
- Actual 2D/3D libraries in use.
- Current timeline/state formats.
- Existing AI endpoints and command grammars.
- Browser routes that can be tested.
- Existing tests and scripts.
- Import graph around movie code.
